raw_response:
I found four transferable mechanisms for selecting a function or method as a value while keeping the reference short.

1. Objective-C compound selector literals and SEL values
https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/Cocoa/Conceptual/ObjectiveC/Chapters/ocSelectors.html

Objective-C selector literals preserve the complete keyword name without argument values or parameter types, providing a direct model for distinguishing label-different methods and passing the selected name to an external object runtime. This is the closest fit for both compound-name spelling and runtime interoperability. A SEL identifies a name, however, rather than a bound implementation or typed function value; receiver binding and signature checking need separate rules. The opened archived chapter is dated 2013-04-23.

2. Scala named-argument placeholder anonymous functions
https://docs.scala-lang.org/sips/1.html

Scala's named-argument placeholder functions suggest a compact adapter syntax that preserves the desired argument labels while constructing a callable without a handwritten forwarding body. This offers a plausible alternative based on an abbreviated call expression instead of a dedicated name literal. The documented examples still require an expected function type or an explicit placeholder type, and the evidence does not establish label-only overloading. The exact live page is undated, so I mark this evidence unknown relative to the cutoff; a 2010 presentation and the Scala 2.8 release record establish historical named-argument support but do not independently date the exact placeholder example.

3. Squeak Smalltalk interned keyword-selector symbols
https://wiki.squeak.org/squeak/uploads/SqueakLanguageRef.3.html

Squeak's interned keyword-selector symbols provide a compact value representation in which every label segment participates in the selector's identity, helping represent and compare full method names independently of argument types. This is useful for the underlying name representation and lookup keys. A symbol alone is not a typed callable and does not capture a receiver, so static resolution, binding, and ambiguity diagnostics remain necessary. The opened reference is version 1.2, dated 2001-04-26.

4. Erlang function references qualified by name and arity
https://www.erlang.org/docs/17/pdf/otp-system-documentation.pdf

Erlang's fun Name/Arity and fun Module:Name/Arity forms show how a small amount of identifying information can construct a function value while eliminating a repetitive forwarding closure. The official manual explicitly relates the local form to an anonymous function that forwards its arguments. Arity alone cannot distinguish equal-arity methods whose labels differ; it is useful as a grammar and desugaring precedent, not a complete solution to that requirement. The opened manual is dated 2015-03-31.

The most directly applicable design combination is a compound name that retains labels, with a separately specified conversion into a callable or external-runtime selector. The Scala mechanism supplies an alternative worth comparing when abbreviated adapter expressions are preferable. These are proposed transfers from existing mechanisms; no claim is made that they were deployed or proved useful for this problem.
